Complete Segal Spaces

Diogo Andrade

Composable arrows and coherent triangles

Let XXX be a Reedy fibrant simplicial space. The space of arrows from xxx to yyy is the fiber map⁡X(x,y)\operatorname{map}_X(x,y)mapX​(x,y) of the endpoint map from X1X_1X1​ to X0×X0X_0\times X_0X0​×X0​. A coherent triangle in X2X_2X2​ records a composable pair, a third edge, and the coherence between them.

Restriction to the spine of the 222-simplex gives the map

(d2,d0):X2⟶X1×X0X1. (d_2,d_0):X_2\longrightarrow X_1\times_{X_0}X_1. (d2​,d0​):X2​⟶X1​×X0​​X1​.
The right-hand side records two arrows with matching endpoints. Reedy fibrancy makes this restriction a fibration. To see this, restrict first to the boundary of the triangle, and then forget the third edge. The first map is the matching fibration. The second is a pullback of the endpoint fibration for X1X_1X1​.

The Segal condition says, more generally, that restriction to the spine gives an equivalence

Xn≃X1×X0⋯×X0X1⏟n factors X_n\simeq \underbrace{X_1\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}X_1}_{n\text{ factors}} Xn​≃n factorsX1​×X0​​⋯×X0​​X1​​​
for every n≥2n\geq 2n≥2. Thus the degree-two map is a trivial fibration. For a pair (f,g)(f,g)(f,g) of composable arrows, its fiber is the space of choices of a coherent composite. This fiber is contractible. Restricting a triangle in the fiber along d1d_1d1​ gives an arrow from the source of fff to the target of ggg.

The higher Segal maps express the same principle for longer strings. They keep track of the coherence of compositions with three or more factors.

Completeness

Let Xeq⊆X1X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1Xeq​⊆X1​ be the union of components consisting of arrows that are equivalences in the homotopy category of XXX. The completeness condition asks that the identity degeneracy

s0:X0⟶Xeq s_0:X_0\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm{eq}} s0​:X0​⟶Xeq​
be an equivalence. This makes paths in the object space reflect equivalences between objects. The argument for composition above already takes place at the level of Segal spaces.

See Contractibility as Uniqueness for the analogous argument using Kan complexes and its connection with a center of contraction.
